public_rationale: Under the ordinary reading that general, robust alignment remained unresolved with substantial technical gaps, the claim is supported. January 2024 experiments showed that standard safety training could fail to remove deliberately implanted deceptive behavior. Earlier research documented progress, but also distinguished those results from solving general alignment. The evidence supports an unresolved technical problem, not a claim that no useful progress had occurred.
limitations: The decisive study was a preprint using deliberately constructed backdoors.
It does not establish spontaneous deception in deployed systems or inevitable catastrophic harm.
The evidence does not quantify how far researchers were from a solution.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI alignment problem is not remotely solved.

statement.excerpt: And, let’s be honest folks, the “alignment problem” isn’t remotely solved.
statement.document_title: Seven reasons why the world should say No to Sam Altman

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that reliably keeping advanced AI systems aligned with intended human goals remained an unresolved problem with substantial technical gaps.
Remotely expresses the seriousness of the remaining gaps; it does not supply a measurable distance to a solution or imply that no progress existed.
The surrounding discussion of scaling and catastrophic risks makes general, robust alignment the relevant scope, rather than success on a single preference benchmark.
There is no reporting cadence or explicit period. I assess the current early-2024 research state from January 1 through the February 10 post; earlier work is context only.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous primary research demonstrates substantial unresolved failures in robust alignment methods, consistent with the absence of a general reliable solution.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous, independently validated evidence establishes a general alignment method that reliably controls advanced systems across relevant adversarial and unfamiliar conditions.

This supports the ordinary reading that general alignment remained unresolved, without proving that deployed models spontaneously developed such behavior.

evidence.explanation: This earlier disclosure explains the general, scalable problem under discussion. Its date prevents it from independently settling the early-2024 observation.

OpenAI reported progress on a simplified supervision problem, while describing important limitations and differences from aligning superhuman systems. This cautions against reading Marcus as denying all progress, but does not establish a general solution.
